review_comments: [team convention] Round money only with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent). Python's round() and a bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and give wrong invoice totals.

item.title: Use the project's money rounding helper for any monetary result
item.description: The first attempt returned an unrounded Decimal division and was rejected because the team requires ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent).
item.content: Before returning any monetary Decimal, check the repo's money module for a rounding helper (e.g. round_money) and wrap the final value with it. Python's round() and bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.

item.title: Read the money module and existing helpers before implementing
item.description: Inspecting ledgerly/money.py revealed ZERO, to_money, and round_money, which the accepted solution reused instead of raw arithmetic.
item.content: When a task involves amounts, open the money/utility module first and reuse its constants and converters (ZERO, to_money, round_money) so behavior matches the rest of the codebase.

item.title: Handle the empty/zero-denominator case explicitly
item.description: The accepted implementation returns ZERO when total quantity is zero, avoiding a division-by-zero for invoices without lines.
item.content: For weighted-average or ratio computations, sum the denominator first and return the module's zero constant when it is zero, rather than relying on the caller or catching exceptions.
